subject: Clarify hosting path for HIPAA workloads — preflight questions & checklist
messages:
From: Julia Ramos <julia@hearthwayhealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: Adam Lee <adam.lee@hearthwayhealth.com>
Date: 2027-11-29T16:20:00-05:00
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's discovery — HIPAA / hosting preference

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the call this morning — we appreciated the clear breakdown of hosting modes. A few quick items from our side so we can pull internal approvers together: 

- We need a succinct checklist (one page) that maps Redwood's hosted vs dedicated vs private options to compliance controls (BAA eligibility, SOC2 evidence you can provide, data residency constraints).
- We will likely handle PHI and prefer a VPC or on-prem option if the compliance burden is harder with hosted; want to understand the trade-offs and what evidence/attestations you can provide up-front.
- Our security team asked for an expected QPS and token volume example so they can size the network controls for the private path. Ballpark today: 25 req/s peak, average 8–10 req/s, ~1200 tokens per request during peak.

Attached is a short risk-profile workbook we use (redacted). Can you confirm which of the three hosting modes would be eligible for a BAA right away and what SOC2 artifacts Redwood can share without an NDA?

Two asks for next steps: 
1) short checklist comparing options we can share with our procurement and security folks,
2) a short list of the specific evidence we can expect (SOC2 Type II, penetration test summary, audit scope, logging/audit log retention).

Appreciate it — can we target a short follow-up email tomorrow with those items and a follow-up 30-min call next week?

Best,
Julia Ramos
Head of Compliance
Hearthway Health

---

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Julia Ramos <julia@hearthwayhealth.com>
Cc: Adam Lee <adam.lee@hearthwayhealth.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T09:08:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery — HIPAA / hosting preference

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear summary and the workbook. Good notes from the call. Below is a concise preflight checklist and the evidence we can provide without an NDA. I also included the trade-offs to help your security/procurement decide.

Short checklist (one-page summary):
- BAA eligibility: Hosted API (yes, with BAA for enterprise agreements), Dedicated (yes, standard for reserved capacity contracts), Private VPC / on-prem (yes, supported via our Private offering).
- SOC2 evidence we can provide immediately (redacted): SOC2 Type II report summary, Security control matrix, Pen test summary (high-level). Full SOC2 report or penetration test artifacts require PO or existing PII NDA in place for sensitive attachments.
- Data residency: All three options support region pinning (us-east-1, us-west-2). Private/on-prem allows complete customer-controlled data plane.
- Audit logs & retention: Hosted: 90 days by default (longer retention add-on available). Dedicated: configurable up to 365 days. Private: customer-controlled retention policy.
- Network controls / connectivity: Hosted: TLS + mTLS for customer integrations; Dedicated: private peering options; Private: VPC peering / direct connect or on-prem VPN.
- Scaling & latency trade-offs: Hosted fastest to onboard; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-request variability; Private maximizes isolation but requires ops and network configuration.

Evidence we can attach now (redacted high-level docs):
- SOC2_TypeII_Redacted.pdf (summary)
- BAA_template.docx (standard agreement)
- PenTest_Summary (redacted excerpt)

Sizing note for your QPS: with 25 req/s peak and ~1.2k tokens/request, Dedicated or Private are the recommended paths if you need steady tail-latency guarantees and predictable unit economics. Hosted is possible for early pilots but expect higher variance unless you reserve dedicated capacity or enable burst/commit options.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I will send the one-page checklist and attach the redacted SOC2 summary and BAA template (below).
2) Internal ask: please confirm compliance reviewers and whether we can exchange an NDA/PO to unlock full artifacts; if yes, we'll push the full SOC2 to the secure drive.
3) Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up on Tuesday 2027-12-07 10:00–10:30 ET to walk the procurement/security team through the checklist?

I will loop in our security lead (Sergio) and account lead (Ben) for technical follow-up and pricing.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0182

Attachments: SOC2_TypeII_Redacted.pdf (stub), BAA_template.docx (stub)
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com

Date: 2027-11-30T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: Hearthway — hosting preflight & SOC2/BAA asks (need quick ops input)

Sergio / Ben — forwarding Julia's workbook and the checklist I just sent. Quick asks so we can respond by EOD: 

Sergio: can you confirm the exact SOC2/pen test excerpts we can upload without an NDA, and whether we can shorten the SOC2 summary to a one-page control mapping (Redwood control -> Hearthway requirement)? Also note: they asked about audit log retention defaults for Dedicated vs Hosted — current defaults are 90d hosted / up to 365d dedicated; private is customer-controlled. If you can prod Security to OK the redacted full SOC2 to the secure Drive under a PO/NDA, that'll unblock procurement.

Ben: can you run a quick Dedicated vs Private pricing sketch for 25 req/s peak, assuming 2x headroom, 30-day run estimate and include an upfront commit option vs pay-as-you-go? Assume US region. We want two simple numbers: monthly committed cost (reserved) and monthly private VPC estimate (managed).

Hearthway is leaning toward Private VPC because of PHI, but they'd like clear trade-offs and a BAA. I've attached their RiskProfile workbook.

I'll draft a one-page checklist and an email template for procurement to sign the BAA/PO. Please send replies inline and copy me.

Thanks,
Olga
